facts.what_happened: In 2011 the Supervisor Two, Billing and Customer Accounts position (formerly Marlene's) came open after a reclass.
Doreen brought the speaker a congratulations card before he applied.
The speaker did not submit an application.
HR posted the job; the speaker took the packet home; it sat in the door pocket of his truck for eleven days.
The speaker filled out most of the application at the kitchen table in pen.
Section Six asked him to describe supervisory philosophy and give an example of addressing a performance issue, with half a page of lines.
The speaker never wrote anything in Section Six.
On the deadline day, he drove past the admin building on his lunch break and kept going.
He went to Arby's.

He told Tammy that night the reasons: $4,200/year raise before taxes, about $200/month after PERS pickup and tax bracket change, loss of overtime eligibility, Nathan's travel ball trip to Cooperstown that summer, and being on call for main breaks.
Tammy said okay and did not push.
Brad Nusser, 31, from the engineering side, got the position.
The speaker trained Brad, sitting with him for about six weeks.
Brad has been the speaker's boss for about fifteen years.
Brad brings the speaker a Dairy Queen cake on his anniversary date every year.
Around 2014 or 2015, Brad conducted a corrective action on Cheryl Vandersteen (18 years at the company) over time card issues, and the speaker was the department witness.
The meeting took place in a small conference room with a whiteboard nobody erases, lasting forty minutes.
Cheryl cried during the meeting, then returned to her desk and worked her full afternoon, answering phones, two rows from the speaker.
The speaker still has the unsubmitted application.
The application is stored in a gray filing cabinet in the garage, second drawer, with snowblower manuals.
Tammy found the application a couple years back while cleaning the garage, held it up without speaking, the speaker said to throw it out, and she put it back in the drawer.
The same cabinet contains receipts from a Buick the family sold in 2009.
